newsitem.title: USA: Pemex propane appetite sated by Saudis-trader.
newsitem.headline: Pemex propane appetite sated by Saudis-trader.

text.p: A top trader for Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) denied industry talk that the monopoly will return to spot international propane markets because of a supply gap left by the July blast at its Cactus plant.

In an interview late Friday, the Mexico City-based trader, who wished to remain anonymous, said Pemex has enough propane to meet domestic demand under a recent contract with Saudi Arabia. Cactus is a natural gas processing plant in southern Mexico.
"What Cactus is not producing is going to be replaced by the Saudi cargoes and we will probably have one or two cargoes left over to sell in March," estimated the source.
Pemex signed a contract with Saudi Arabia in August for 500,000 barrels of propane per month from September to March.
But last week, several U.S. traders and analysts said the monopoly will still need more in order to cover Mexico's winter demand, which begins in late November.

The first of the Saudi cargoes is expected to arrive in early October and, according to the Pemex source, will be delivered straight into underground storage in Mont Belvieu, Texas, on the U.S. Gulf Coast.
"We will be bringing propane into Mexico City depending on Mexico's needs," said the trader, adding the company has already begun to sell barrels that were in Belvieu storage.
"Over the past two weeks we've sold small prompt parcels, totalling about 300,000 barrels," said the source, adding Pemex tried to sell more on Friday for 49.00 cents but found no buyers.
U.S. traders have confirmed buying Pemex barrels, but some were unsure if Pemex was long or was trying to lower the cost of extra imports it may need in the near future.

The Pemex trader, however, said, that about 50 percent of Cactus' production capacity is back on stream, producing about 22,500 barrels per day of LPGs from the portion undamaged by the July 26 blaze.
The source said he does not expect the plant to reach its pre-explosion capacity of between 50,000 to 70,000 bpd until late next year.
But our needs will still be met by Cactus and other refiners and producers in Mexico and by storage we already have in Belvieu," said the trader.
He said Mexico's current total production is about 185,000 bpd, compared to the pre-explosion total capacity of about 270,000 bpd.
He added imports of natural gas since the explosion have also dropped, to 53 million cubic feet per day from the 303 mcf imported in August following the blast.
